creator: Hacer Ceren Tokgoz, Barkin Kultursay, Seda Tanyeri, Dicle Sırma, Cagdas Bulus, Tezel Kovanci, Mustafa Kara, Seyma Zeynep Atici, Seyma Nur Cicek, Caglar Emre Cagliyan, Azmican Kaya, Faruk Akalin, Dogan Sen, Leyla Aliyeva, Nihal Ozdemir, Cihangir Kaymaz
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Risk stratification is essential in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), yet the prognostic utility of the albumin‐bilirubin (ALBI) score as a marker of hepatic dysfunction remains underexplored. In this single‐center study, we evaluated the clinical, neurohumoral, echocardiographic and hemodynamic correlates and prognostic value of the ALBI score, and to assess whether this score offers an incremental benefit over the Registry to EValuate Early And Long‐term pulmonary arterial hypertension disease management (REVEAL) 2.0 risk score in patients with PAH.

title: Age‐Period‐Cohort Analysis of the Global Death Burden of Main Diseases Attributable to High Temperature in the Past 30 Years: Based on the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021
creator: Zhikang Wang, Yifang Liu, Lve Deng, Ke Li, Jiawei Ren, Xuran Shi, Qi Wang, Junan Liu
description: High temperatures pose a serious threat to human health. Quantifying the main disease death burden attributable to high temperatures can provide scientific evidence for policy development. Using Global Burden of Disease 2021 data, we identified the death burden attributable to high temperatures across all causes and determined the three leading causes.

title: Editorial: Micro and nanoparticles for regenerative medicine
creator: Aurore Van de Walle, Yang Zhang, Alessandro Polini, Riccardo Di Corato
description: race against bacterial resistance is becoming pressing. Particles in the micrometer or nanometer range provide original, size-dependent, and tunable physiochemical features. This Research Topic “Micro- and Nano-Particles for Regenerative Medicine” reports on creative syntheses, compositions, and applications of these biomaterials.

title: Distinct Rates and Transmission Patterns of Major HIV-1 Subtypes among Men who Have Sex with Men in Guangxi, China
creator: Xianwu Pang, Bo Xie, Qin He, Xing Xie, Jinghua Huang, Kailing Tang, Ningye Fang, Haoming Xie, Jie Ma, Xianmin Ge, Guanghua Lan, Shujia Liang
description: The diversity and transmission patterns of major HIV-1 subtypes among MSM population in Guangxi remains unknown. Understanding the characteristics is crucial for effective intervention strategies. Between 2016 and 2021, we recruited individuals newly diagnosed with HIV-1 from MSM population in Guangxi.

title: Cancer-cell-mimicking MnO2 nanoplatform delivers immunological adjuvants to enhance radio-immunotherapy
creator: Zhen Zhang, Ping Liu, Weike Zeng, Chunlin Huang, Siqing Wang, Shiyao Guan, Yixi Duan, Dalin Wu, Yi Zhao, Jun Wu
description: The hypoxic and immunosuppressive microenvironment within tumors represents a fundamental mechanism contributing to radiotherapy (RT) resistance, which is closely linked to poor prognosis in cancer patients. To overcome these limitations, we constructed a tumor cell membrane-mimetic manganese-based nanoplatform for delivering immune adjuvants (MnO2-R848@CM) to synergistically enhance the efficacy of clinical radiotherapy.

title: AI-assisted neurocognitive assessment protocol for older adults with psychiatric disorders
creator: Diego D. Díaz-Guerra, Marena de la C. Hernández-Lugo, Yunier Broche-Pérez, Carlos Ramos-Galarza, Ernesto Iglesias-Serrano, Zoylen Fernández-Fleites
description: IntroductionEvaluating neurocognitive functions and diagnosing psychiatric disorders in older adults is challenging due to the complexity of symptoms and individual differences. An innovative approach that combines the accuracy of artificial intelligence (AI) with the depth of neuropsychological assessments is needed.

title: Preclinical characterization of CPL304110 as a potent and selective inhibitor of fibroblast growth factor receptors 1, 2, and 3 for gastric, bladder, and squamous cell lung cancer
creator: Delfina Popiel, Aleksandra Stańczak, Monika Skupińska, Agata Mikołajczyk, Paulina Stańczak, Filip Mituła, Joanna Hucz-Kalitowska, Kinga Jastrzębska, Damian Smuga, Jakub Dominowski, Monika Delis, Krzysztof Mulewski, Wojciech Pietruś, Daria Zdżalik-Bielecka, Karolina Dzwonek, Monika Lamparska-Przybysz
description: Fibroblast Growth Factor Receptors (FGFRs) are a family of receptor tyrosine kinases expressed on a plethora of cell membranes. They play crucial roles in both embryonic development and adult tissue functions. There is an increasing amount of evidence that FGFR-mediated oncogenesis is mainly related to gene amplification, activating mutations, or translocation in tumors of various histological types.

title: A Test for the Profession: Medicine in Nazi Germany
creator: Michael Trimble
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In this paper I will chart the development of the medical sub-culture within Nazi German society. I intend to show that ethical regulation provided by professional societies, state, and the legal system were inadequate and failed to prevent the atrocities perpetrated by Nazi doctors and that the acceptance of the concept of “a life not worth living” was a key turning point in medical culture and practice. A testing question How might ethical standards be upheld?

title: The impact of long-term care insurance on the health status and healthcare expenditure of older adults in China
creator: Ran An, Shujie Xiu, Xiaosheng Yang, Shishi Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveLong-term care needs have grown with population aging. This study explores the relationships among health status, healthcare expenditure, and long-term care insurance (LTCI) among the older adults.MethodsUsing data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS 2011, 2013, 2015, 2018, and 2020) and based on the demand model for healthcare services, this study employed the difference-in-difference (DID) method to assess how the implementation of LTCI contributed to the health status and healthcare expenditures of the older adults.

title: Microvascular Reconstruction in Ballistic Injuries of the Maxillofacial Region
creator: Michael Maurer, Katja Himmelstoss, Nura Ahmad, Mathias Fiedler, Johannes G. Schuderer, Johannes K. Meier, Torsten E. Reichert, Tobias Ettl
description: Background:Ballistic injuries to the maxillofacial region pose a major reconstructive challenge due to complex anatomy and the need to restore both aesthetic appearance and essential functions such as speech and swallowing. This study evaluates microvascular reconstruction strategies and associated complications in these injuries.

title: Current advances in biomaterials for inner ear cell regeneration
creator: Junze Lu, Man Wang, Yu Meng, Weibin An, Xue Wang, Gaoying Sun, Haibo Wang, Wenwen Liu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Inner ear cell regeneration from stem/progenitor cells provides potential therapeutic strategies for the restoration of sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL), however, the efficiency of regeneration is low and the functions of differentiated cells are not yet mature. Biomaterials have been used in inner ear cell regeneration to construct a more physiologically relevant 3D culture system which mimics the stem cell microenvironment and facilitates cellular interactions. Currently, these biomaterials include hydrogel, conductive materials, magneto-responsive materials, photo-responsive materials, etc.

title: Postbiotics Unveiled: The Next Emerging Trend in Functional Foods
creator: Zoha Wahid, Abdul Momin Rizwan Ahmad, Farheen Zulfiqar, Syed Hassan Bin Usman Shah, Nilab Mohammadi
description: The global population is expected to reach 9.7 billion by 2050, with demand for food increasing by up to 56%. Postbiotics are a safe and reliable substitute for probiotics, which are described as preparations of non‐viable bacteria and/or their metabolic byproducts. Data for this narrative review was collected using Goggle scholar and PubMed from 2006 to 2026.

title: Virgo-inspired Periorbital Lifting Injection Technique: A Structured Multinodal, Layered Framework for Periorbital Rejuvenation
creator: Jiajia Li, Yongping Xue, Letian Kuang, Qianyi Wu, Wenrong Tian, Suriye Rehemutila, Jiang Ai
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Summary:Periorbital aging extends beyond isolated volume loss and encompasses progressive changes in structural support, contour continuity, and tissue transition. These changes often produce a segmented or fatigued appearance that may not be adequately corrected by focal filling alone. We describe the Virgo-inspired periorbital lifting injection technique as a structured, multinodal, layered framework that organizes recognized periorbital support and transition zones into a reproducible treatment sequence.

title: Improving panicle blast resistance and fragrance in a high-quality japonica rice variety through breeding
creator: Junhua Ye, Kai Wang, Yi Wang, Zhipeng Zhao, Ying Yan, Hang Yang, Lixia Zhang, Zejun Hu, Zhenying Shi, Dapeng Sun, Jianjiang Bai, Liming Cao, Shujun Wu
description: IntroductionHuruan1212 (HR1212) is well-regarded for its superior eating and cooking quality in the lower reaches of the Yangtze River in China. Still, its high susceptibility to rice panicle blast and lack of fragrance have limited its further spread and utilization.

title: Reflex‐Mediated Bradycardia and Asystole During Skull Base and Parapharyngeal Surgery: A Three‐Case Series Highlighting Anatomical Predictability
creator: Songyuan Chi, Yiru Wang, Xia Shen
description: Intraoperative bradycardia and asystole during cranial neurovascular surgery are often regarded as unexpected events. In clinical practice, however, these episodes may occur during manipulation of specific cranial nerve‐rich anatomical regions, suggesting that the risk may be anticipated and clinically actionable.

title: Spatial, temporal, and spatiotemporal cluster detection of malaria incidence in Southwest Ethiopia
creator: Lidetu Demoze, Fetlework Gubena, Eyob Akalewold, Helen Brhan, Tigist Kifle, Gelila Yitageasu
description: BackgroundMalaria is a major global health hazard, particularly in developing countries such as Ethiopia, where it contributes to high morbidity and mortality rates. According to reports from the South Omo Zone Health Bureau, despite various interventions such as insecticide-treated bed nets and indoor residual spraying, the incidence of malaria has increased in recent years.

title: Icariin modulates osteogenic and adipogenic differentiation in ADSCs via the Hippo-YAP/TAZ pathway: a novel therapeutic strategy for osteoporosis
creator: Shaozi Lin, Zuyu Meng, Mei Wang, Zixuan Ye, Mengsha Long, Yiyao Zhang, Fang Liu, Hongling Chen, Menghan Li, Jiajia Qin, Haiquan Liu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundAdipose-derived stem cell (ADSC) transplantation presents a promising approach for osteoporosis (OP) treatment. However, the therapeutic efficacy of ADSCs is hindered by low post-transplantation survival rates and limited capacities for adhesion, migration, and differentiation.

title: Intruders or protectors – the multifaceted role of B cells in CNS disorders
creator: James W. Aspden, Matthew A. Murphy, Rommi D. Kashlan, Yueyue Xiong, Mark C. Poznansky, Ruxandra F. Sîrbulescu
description: B lymphocytes are immune cells studied predominantly in the context of peripheral humoral immune responses against pathogens. Evidence has been accumulating in recent years on the diversity of immunomodulatory functions that B cells undertake, with particular relevance for pathologies of the central nervous system (CNS).

title: Genetic variation in patent foramen ovale: a case-control genome-wide association study
creator: Bosi Dong, Yajiao Li, Fandi Ai, Jia Geng, Ting Tang, Wan Peng, Yusha Tang, Hui Wang, Zixuan Tian, Fengxiao Bu, Lei Chen
description: BackgroundPatent foramen ovale (PFO) is a congenital defect between the atria, resulting in abnormal hemodynamics. We conducted a genome-wide association study (GWAS) to identify common genetic variants associated with PFO.MethodsWe performed a whole genome sequencing in a discovery cohort of 3,227 unrelated Chinese participants screened for PFO via contrast transthoracic echocardiography (cTTE).

title: Short-term effects of foot surgery on walking-related pain, function, and satisfaction in patients with Charcot–Marie–Tooth disease: a prospective cohort study
creator: Giacomo Basini, Chiara Rambelli, Martina Galletti, Paolo Zerbinati, Paolo Prati, Francesca Mascioli, Stefano Masiero, Davide Mazzoli, Andrea Merlo
description: IntroductionPatients with Charcot–Marie–Tooth disease (CMT) often suffer from walking-related pain (WRP), muscle weakness, foot deformities, and reduced ankle dorsiflexion (DF), which affects their ability to walk and daily activities. Functional surgery (FS) can restore foot deviations, affecting the loading ability during gait.

title: A deep learning model for carotid plaques detection based on CTA images: a two stepwise early-stage clinical validation study
creator: Zhongping Guo, Ying Liu, Jingxu Xu, Chencui Huang, Fandong Zhang, Chongchang Miao, Yonggang Zhang, Mengshuang Li, Hangsheng Shan, Yan Gu
description: ObjectiveTo develop a deep learning (DL) model for carotid plaque detection based on CTA images and evaluate the clinical application feasibility and value of the model.MethodsWe retrospectively collected data from patients with carotid atherosclerotic plaques who underwent continuous CTA examinations of the head and neck at a tertiary hospital from October 2020 to October 2022.

title: Altered amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation and functional connectivity in patients with acute unilateral vestibulopathy: a resting-state fMRI study
creator: Zhengwei Chen, Liangqun Rong, Lijie Xiao, Jie Rao, Haiyan Liu, Tengfei Liu, Fei Chen, Jun Zhang, Lu Wang, Xi Li, Xiue Wei
description: ObjectiveTo investigate changes of brain functional activity in patients with acute unilateral vestibulopathy (AUVP) using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI).MethodsWe studied 32 AUVP patients and 30 healthy controls (HC) who received resting-state fMRI scanning. Methods of voxel-based amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (ALFF) and seed-based functional connectivity (FC) were adopted to compare the difference in brain function between the two groups.

title: Safety evaluation of the food enzyme endo‐polygalacturonase from the non‐genetically modified Rhizopus oryzae strain MC3‐3‐9
creator: EFSA Panel on Food Enzymes (FEZ), Holger Zorn, José Manuel Barat Baviera, Claudia Bolognesi, Francesco Catania, Gabriele Gadermaier, Ralf Greiner, Baltasar Mayo, Alicja Mortensen, Yrjö Henrik Roos, Marize L M Solano, Henk Van Loveren, Laurence Vernis, Cristina Andreoli, Andrea Terron, Andrey Yurkov,
description: The food enzyme endo‐polygalacturonase (1,4‐α‐D‐galacturonan glycanohydrolase, EC 3.2.1.15) is produced with the non‐genetically modified Rhizopus oryzae strain MC3‐3‐9 by Shin Nihon Chemical Co., Ltd. The food enzyme was considered free from viable cells of the production organism. It is intended to be used in five food manufacturing processes.

title: Epigenetic modulation of antitumor immunity and immunotherapy response in breast cancer: biological mechanisms and clinical implications
creator: Jun Yin, Tiezheng Gu, Norin Chaudhry, Nancy E. Davidson, Yi Huang
description: Breast cancer (BC) is the most common non-skin cancer and the second leading cause of cancer death in American women. The initiation and progression of BC can proceed through the accumulation of genetic and epigenetic changes that allow transformed cells to escape the normal cell cycle checkpoint control.

title: Multidisciplinary Management of a Giant Ovarian Sertoli–Leydig Cell Tumor Presenting With Isosexual Precocious Puberty: A Pediatric Case Report
creator: Sanaa Bouramdane, Kenza Elmkaddem, Nawal Hammas, Meryem Boubbou, Othmane Alaoui, Khalid Khattala, Youssef Bouabdellah, Sarra Benmiloud
description: Sertoli–Leydig cell tumors (SLCTs) are rare ovarian sex cord‐stromal tumors, particularly uncommon in the pediatric population. They are typically androgen‐secreting, while estrogen‐secreting forms are rare and may lead to diagnostic confusion with granulosa cell tumors. We report the case of a 7‐year‐old girl presenting with progressive abdominal distension and isosexual precocious puberty.

title: Case report: Intra-abdominal inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor with mucinous features: a case of rapid recurrence and dissemination post-surgery
creator: Xingchen Li, Jie Li, Chunxiao Liang, Qing Zou
description: Inflammatory myofibroblastic tumors (IMTs) are rare mesenchymal neoplasms with intermediate biological potential and are characterized by spindle-shaped myofibroblastic cells and significant inflammatory infiltrates. This case report describes a 24-year-old male with diabetes who was admitted to the hospital for over three days of vomiting and abdominal pain and was initially diagnosed with diabetic ketoacidosis.

title: Human erythroid models of sickle cell disease
creator: Deborah E. Daniels, Maria A. Lizarralde‐Iragorri, Fatima O. Oyawoye, David C. Rees, Jan Frayne, Sara El Hoss
description: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a group of severe inherited red blood cell disorders causing a major global healthcare burden. Despite recent advances in gene therapy and stem cell transplantation, treatment options remain very limited, highlighting the urgent need for the development of new therapeutic approaches.

title: Ligustrum × vicaryi Fruit Polysaccharide Attenuates LPS/D-GalN-Induced Acute Liver Injury in Mice
creator: Shu-Ling Liu, Hui Zhang, Jian-An Wang, Run-Dong Lv, Shao-Jian Li, Li-Tao Wang
description: The dried fruits of Ligustrum lucidum Ait. are well-established in East Asian medicine for hepatoprotection. Given this ethnopharmacological precedent and their close taxonomic kinship, we hypothesized that the fruit polysaccharide of its horticultural congener, Ligustrum × vicaryi L. (LVFP), may confer analogous hepatic benefits.

title: Editorial: COVID-19 epidemiological situation as a psychosocial determinant of trauma and stress
creator: Mateusz Grajek, Ewa Misterska, Jonathan Adedayo Odukoya, Mateusz Rozmiarek
description: /or those with underlying chronic comorbidities, experienced the development of severe bilateral pneumonia, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and consequently, multiorgan dysfunction, potentially leading to mortality (Yong, 2021; Merad et al., 2022). Consequently, the fear of infection, especially the severe course of the disease and death, undoubtedly became a cause of generalized anxiety and fear for many individuals (Gunnell et al.

title: Sleep-Gated Adaptation: A Conceptual Framework Linking Exercise-Induced Adaptive Consolidation to Interindividual Variability in Training Response
creator: Teodora Dominteanu, Amelia Elena Stan, Andreea Voinea
description: Exercise-induced molecular signaling is transient, resolving within hours, whereas the structural and functional adaptations to repeated training develop over weeks to months. The processes that convert signaling into durable adaptation, the conditions that best support this conversion, and the sources of interindividual variability in training outcomes have largely been studied separately.

title: Subhepatic appendicitis in a 27-year-old male: a case report from Odahulle General Hospital of Ethiopia
creator: Abduletif Haji Ababor Abagojam, Remedan Jemal Dekema, Tamirat Godebo Woyimo, Jafer Yasin Mohammed, Kedir Negesso Tukeni
description: The appendix is a small, tube-shaped organ that connects to the cecum, the beginning of the large intestine. Though its role is unknown, it can become infected, resulting in acute appendicitis, which, if not detected and treated early, can lead to serious consequences.

title: Construction of shared gene signature between rheumatoid arthritis and lung adenocarcinoma helps to predict the prognosis and tumor microenvironment of the LUAD patients
creator: Liping Shi, Houwen Zou, Jian Yi
description: Introduction: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a common chronic autoimmune disease with high incidence rate and high disability rate. One of the top complications is cancer, especially lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). However, the molecular mechanisms linking RA and LUAD are still not clear.

title: Effects of cellulose nanocrystals on the physicochemical and retrogradation properties of pea starch
creator: Shaoning Cui, Shaoqian Cui, Wei Xie, Hui Li, Fang Li, Shengju Ge, Zhaoquan Fu, Han Du
description: Pea starch (PS), with its high amylose content, is prone to retrogradation, which limits the shelf life of pea-based foods. However, direct evidence linking the dispersion of cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) to water-state changes in high-amylose legume starch remains limited. The gelation and storage-induced reorganization of PS with 0–8% CNCs were investigated by multi-scale analyses.

title: Conduction system pacing using electro-anatomical mapping-guided system vs. fluoroscopy: a systematic review, meta-analysis and economic evaluation
creator: Beatriz León-Salas, Diego Infante-Ventura, Aránzazu Hernández-Yumar, Renata Linertová, Estefanía Herrera-Ramos, Alezandra Torres-Castaño, Himar González-Pacheco, Analía Abt-Sacks, Javier García-García, Raúl Quirós-López, María M. Trujillo-Martín
description: IntroductionElectro-anatomical mapping (EAM) system has been shown as an alternative procedure to fluoroscopy for conduction system pacing (CSP) in patients with severe bradyarrhythmia, however its beneficial and harmful effects has not been assessed in a systematic review (SR). We sought to assess their safety, effectiveness and cost-effectiveness.

title: Setting up the first human milk bank in Uganda: a success story from Nsambya hospital
creator: Victoria Nakibuuka, Janat Kainza, Ritah Nasiima, Sanyu Nalunga, Ritah Nazziwa, Hamim Mponye, Christinah Nuwahereza, Ronald Kyambadde, Racheal Nantenza, Caroline Nassonko, Barbara Nalubwama, Immaculate Nabwami, Madrine Nabaliira, Cleophas Kabategweta, Olivia Nalule, Joannita Nampijja, Barbara Namugga
description: BackgroundThe World Health Organization (WHO) strongly recommends the use of donor human milk (DHM) for low birth weight infants when mother’s own milk is unavailable or insufficient. However, the use of DHM requires the availability of human milk banks (HMBs), the majority of which are in middle and high-income countries.

title: A Market Survey of Pesticide Residues in Fruit Juices in Slovenia in 2026
creator: Helena Baša Česnik
description: Although the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) encourages the monitoring of pesticide residues in food, only 8.4% of processed fruit samples were monitored in the EU in 2023. In addition, the literature mainly focuses on pesticide residues in fruit rather than in juices.

title: Automatic deep learning method for third lumbar selection and body composition evaluation on CT scans of cancer patients
creator: Lidia Delrieu, Damien Blanc, Amine Bouhamama, Fabien Reyal, Frank Pilleul, Victor Racine, Anne Sophie Hamy, Hugo Crochet, Timothée Marchal, Pierre Etienne Heudel
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionThe importance of body composition and sarcopenia is well-recognized in cancer patient outcomes and treatment tolerance, yet routine evaluations are rare due to their time-intensive nature. While CT scans provide accurate measurements, they depend on manual processes. We developed and validated a deep learning algorithm to automatically select and segment abdominal muscles [SM], visceral fat [VAT], and subcutaneous fat [SAT] on CT scans.Materials and MethodsA total of 352 CT scans were collected from two cancer centers.

title: Relationship between ferroptosis and healing of diabetic foot ulcer: a prospective clinical study
creator: Qian Jiang, Long Tang, Shuao Xiao
description: ObjectiveDiabetic foot ulcer (DFU) is one of the common complications in patients with diabetes mellitus (DM). In order to find a method to monitor and treat the refractory DFU, the ferroptosis level in DFU and traumatic wounds (TW) was monitored and the difference between them was analyzed.

title: JAK3-Mediated Structural Remodeling of β-Catenin Suppresses Epithelial–Mesenchymal Transition: Insights from In Silico Modeling
creator: Jugal Kishore Das, Jayshree Mishra, Narendra Kumar
description: Simple SummaryJanus kinase 3 (JAK3) is a non-receptor tyrosine kinase that interacts with and phosphorylates several proteins, including β-catenin, a key component of adherens junctions (AJs). We previously demonstrated that JAK3-mediated phosphorylation of β-catenin regulates its localization to the basolateral membrane and is essential for maintaining epithelial barrier integrity.

title: Citrus transcription factor CsERF1 is involved in the response to citrus tristeza disease
creator: Qi Chen, Fulin Yan, Jing Liu, Zhipeng Xie, Junyao Jiang, Jiamei Liang, Jing Chen, Huanhuan Wang, Jinxiang Liu
description: IntroductionCitrus tristeza virus (CTV) is a threat to the citrus production and causes severe economic losses to the citrus industry. Ethylene response factors (ERFs) play important roles in plant growth and stress responses. Although ERF genes have been widely studied in model plants, little is known about their role in biological stress responses in fruit trees, such as citrus.

title: Friluftsliv literacy—a contribution to physical literacy for health throughout the life course
creator: Eivind Sæther, Idar Lyngstad
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This article illuminates and discusses the concept “friluftsliv literacy” in relation to physical literacy for health throughout the life course. A literal translation into English of “friluftsliv” would be “free-air life” – or “outdoor life.” We obtained stories and interview data from older adult people who could help us by providing insights into friluftsliv literacy through a number of life phases.

title: Integrated Phytoremediation and Microbial Mitigation Strategies for Sustainable Restoration of Toxic Metal-Contaminated Soils
creator: Inès Hammami, Mohamed Abdelaal, Ibtisam M. Ababutain, Sumayah I. Alsanie, Ghadah H. Al Hawas, Azzah I. Alghamdi, Nadiyah M. Alqazlan, Ruba A. Alghamdi, Fajir M. Alsubaie, Joaher Y. Alnabbat
description: Simple SummaryToxic metal contamination of soils poses a global threat because metals such as Cd, Pb, Hg, As, Cr, and Ni threaten ecosystems, food security, and human health. Although conventional remediation methods are effective, they may cause secondary pollution or soil degradation. Biological approaches such as phytoremediation and microbial mitigation are more sustainable but perform inconsistently under field conditions.

title: DIA Quantitative Proteomic Analysis Reveals Early Proteomic Responses to Honeybee-Derived Melittin in Murine Breast Cancer Cells
creator: Junling Zhu, Wenhua Xu, He Zang, Yunzhen Yang, Nian Fan, Yuwei Zhang, Yaqin Gao, Jianfeng Qiu, Dafu Chen, Rui Guo
description: Simple SummaryBreast cancer remains one of the most common cancers worldwide, and the development of new therapeutic approaches is still urgently needed. Melittin, a natural peptide derived from honeybee venom, has attracted attention because of its potential ability to inhibit cancer cells. However, the overall changes occurring inside breast cancer cells after melittin treatment are not fully understood.

title: Comparison of dark-field chest radiography and CT for the assessment of COVID-19 pneumonia
creator: Florian T. Gassert, Henriette Bast, Theresa Urban, Manuela Frank, Felix G. Gassert, Konstantin Willer, Rafael C. Schick, Bernhard Renger, Thomas Koehler, Alexandra Karrer, Andreas P. Sauter, Alexander A. Fingerle, Marcus R. Makowski, Franz Pfeiffer, Daniela Pfeiffer
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundDark-field chest radiography allows the assessment of the structural integrity of the alveoli by exploiting the wave properties of x-rays.PurposeTo compare the qualitative and quantitative features of dark-field chest radiography in patients with COVID-19 pneumonia with conventional CT imaging.Materials and methodsIn this prospective study conducted from May 2020 to December 2020, patients aged at least 18 years who underwent chest CT for clinically suspected COVID-19 infection were screened for participation.

title: LSARE-Net: Target-Guided Augmentation and Lightweight Edge Detection for Real-Time Behavior Monitoring of Captive Juvenile Sika Deer
creator: Xipeng Li, He Pan, Adnan Mahmood, Xin Wang, Tong Yu, Yuncheng Zhao
description: Simple SummaryWhile continuous monitoring can reveal changes in deer behavior, manually reviewing surveillance footage is both time-consuming and labor-intensive. To address this, we developed a camera-based system to detect five behavioral categories in group-housed juvenile sika deer: resting, standing, feeding, social interaction, and abnormal recumbency.

title: Principles, developments, and applications of spatially resolved spectroscopy in agriculture: a review
creator: Yu Xia, Wenxi Liu, Jingwu Meng, Jinghao Hu, Wenbo Liu, Jie Kang, Bin Luo, Han Zhang, Wei Tang
description: Agriculture is the primary source of human survival, which provides the most basic living and survival conditions for human beings. As living standards continue to improve, people are also paying more attention to the quality and safety of agricultural products. Therefore, the detection of agricultural product quality is very necessary.

title: Craving for exercise due to the disruption of daily routine by an earthquake
creator: İsmail İlbak, Ahmet Yasuntimur, Stefan Stojanovic, Serkan Düz, Łukasz Rydzik, Ladislav Cepicka
description: ObjectivesThe research aimed to examine exercise cravings that arise from the disruption of daily routine resulting from the earthquake and the consequent mandatory absence from exercising at fitness centers.Study designThis study utilized the phenomenological design through qualitative research methods.MethodsThe research sample comprises six individuals aged between 22 and 29 years. They were selected using the criterion sampling method.

title: Assessment of genetically modified maize Bt11 × MIR162 × MON 89034 × NK603 (application GMFF‐2025‐33624)
creator: EFSA Panel on Genetically Modified Organisms (GMO), Josep Casacuberta, Francisco Barro, Albert Braeuning, Ruud de Maagd, Michelle M Epstein, Thomas Frenzel, Jean‐Luc Gallois, Frits Koning, Antoine Messéan, F Javier Moreno, Fabien Nogué, Giovanni Savoini, Alan H Schulman, Christoph Tebbe, Eve Veroman
description: Genetically modified maize Bt11 × MIR162 × MON 89034 × NK603 was developed by crossing to combine four single events: Bt11, MIR162, MON 89034 and NK603. The maize Bt11 × MIR162 × MON 89034 × NK603 expresses the Cry1Ab, PAT, Vip3Aa20, PMI, Cry1A.

title: Histopathological and Quantitative Correlates of Intraoperative Narrow Band Imaging in Brain Metastasis Surgery
creator: Tadashi Higuchi, Shinsuke Abe, Satsuki Imaoka, Taisei Aoki, Yohei Nounaka, Atsushi Tsukiyama, Fumihiro Matano, Shigeyuki Tahara, Yasuo Murai
description: Simple SummarySurgeons removing brain tumors that spread from other cancers need a reliable way to see where the tumor ends and healthy brain begins. We tested narrow-band imaging (NBI), a light-based technique that highlights blood vessels without any drug, in a retrospective, exploratory study of 25 patients having brain metastasis surgery.

title: Smart haptic gloves for virtual reality surgery simulation: a pilot study on external ventricular drain training
creator: Jonah Boutin, Jafer Kamoonpuri, Reza Faieghi, Joon Chung, Sandrine de Ribaupierre, Roy Eagleson
description: Smart haptic gloves are a new technology emerging in Virtual Reality (VR) with a promise to enhance sensory feedback in VR. This paper presents one of the first attempts to explore its application to surgical training for neurosurgery trainees using VR-based surgery simulators.

title: Berberine alleviates enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli-induced intestinal mucosal barrier function damage in a piglet model by modulation of the intestinal microbiome
creator: Min Du, Xinran Liu, Xu Ji, Yue Wang, Xiaodan Liu, Chunfang Zhao, Erhui Jin, Youfang Gu, Hongyu Wang, Feng Zhang
description: IntroductionEnterotoxic Escherichia coli (ETEC) is the main pathogen that causes diarrhea, especially in young children. This disease can lead to substantial morbidity and mortality and is a major global health concern. Managing ETEC infections is challenging owing to the increasing prevalence of antibiotic resistance.

title: Radical gastrectomy is safe for treatment of gastric cancer patients on immunosuppressive drugs after organ transplantation
creator: Jin Ah Lee, So Jung Kim, Ho Seok Seo, Han Hong Lee, Sung Geun Kim, Kyong Hwa Jun, Kyo Young Song, Yoon Ju Jung
description: Background De novo malignancies are major causes of death after organ transplantation because the recipients subsequently receive immunosuppressant drugs. When gastric cancer develops, the clinical course of the tumor may be particularly aggressive. However, there are few reliable studies of gastric cancer treatment after organ transplantation.

title: Perspective on the role of norms for institutional behavior and policy design in European cross-border regions
creator: Sara Svensson
description: The article analyses how a norm scientific perspective can advance our understanding of cross-border regions and guide future directions of research. Cross-border regions are territorial spaces comprising territory from two or more national states, located directly at the borders of those spaces.

title: Giant 90-mm Ossified Stylohyoid Chain Associated with Restricted Mouth Opening
creator: Jakub Bargiel, Michał Gontarz, Tomasz Marecik, Krzysztof Gąsiorowski, Grażyna Wyszyńska-Pawelec
description: A 62-year-old man was referred with a six-month history of right submandibular pain followed by dysphagia. At presentation, maximal interincisal opening was 25 mm. Computed tomography angiography demonstrated an ossified right stylohyoid chain extending from the skull base to the hyoid region. It measured 90 mm in length and 17.5 × 10.5 mm at maximal cross-section.

title: Comparing [18F]FET PET and [18F]FDOPA PET for glioma recurrence diagnosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Pengbo Yu, Yinan Wang, Fengbo Su, Yan Chen
description: PurposeThe purpose of our meta-analysis and systematic review was to evaluate and compare the diagnostic effectiveness of [18F]FET PET and [18F]FDOPA PET in detecting glioma recurrence.MethodsSensitivities and specificities were assessed using the DerSimonian and Laird methodology, and subsequently transformed using the Freeman-Tukey double inverse sine transformation.

title: Multi-target regulatory effects of rhaponticin in a rat model of hepatic fibrosis revealed by non-targeted metabolomics
creator: Min Yang, Dihua Jiang, Longfei Huang, Tao Zhang, Wenfen Guo, Wenyan Lin, Jiali Zhao, Yunsheng Wei, Lang Peng, Yong-Jia Hao, Ying Zhou
description: IntroductionHepatic fibrosis (HF), a progressive chronic liver disease, is a serious threat to global public health. The lack of preventive and therapeutic strategies has created an urgent need for effective anti-fibrosis agents. There is growing evidence that natural products might provide safe and effective interventions for HF.

title: The Refugial Squeeze: A Globally Relevant Mechanism of Species Decline Revealed by a Threatened Amphibian
creator: Kate Tunstill, Matt W Hayward, Hannah Power, Darren Southwell, John Gould, Will Farebrother, Michael Mahony, Alex Callen
description: A key outcome of the Global Biodiversity Crisis is the contraction and range shift of species distribution into refugial habitats that afford protection against threatening processes. Range contractions driven by spatially overlapping threats may fragment populations to the point where functional habitat is lost.

title: The characteristics of the tumor immune microenvironment in colorectal cancer with different MSI status and current therapeutic strategies
creator: Qingzhe Wang, Min Yu, Shuang Zhang
description: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a significant cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Despite advancements in surgery, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy, the effectiveness of these conventional treatments is limited, particularly in advanced cases. Therefore, transition to novel treatment is urgently needed. Immunotherapy, especially immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), has shown promise in improving outcomes for CRC patients.

title: Antigen-presenting B cells promote TCF-1+ PD1- stem-like CD8+ T-cell proliferation in glioblastoma
creator: David Hou, Hanxiao Wan, Joshua L. Katz, Si Wang, Brandyn A. Castro, Gustavo I. Vazquez-Cervantes, Victor A. Arrieta, Silpol Dhiantravan, Hinda Najem, Aida Rashidi, Tzu-yi Chia, Tarlan Arjmandi, Jimena Collado, Leah Billingham, Aurora Lopez-Rosas, Yu Han, Adam M. Sonabend, Amy B. Heimberger, Peng Zha
description: Understanding the spatial relationship and functional interaction of immune cells in glioblastoma (GBM) is critical for developing new therapeutics that overcome the highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Our study showed that B and T cells form clusters within the GBM microenvironment within a 15-μm radius, suggesting that B and T cells could form immune synapses within the GBM.

title: Psychologists’ Perspectives of Service-Access Barriers for Syrian Children with Disabilities in a Turkish Refugee Camp
creator: Ibraheem M. Alsawalem, Abdulmalik Alkhunini
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background/Objectives: Syrian refugee children with disabilities face multiple barriers to accessing essential healthcare, education, psychological support, and protection services. These challenges are often compounded by displacement, poverty, language and documentation difficulties, and limited specialized services. This study aimed to explore these barriers and their interrelated challenges exclusively from the perspectives of practitioners working directly with this population within a refugee-camp context.

title: Clinical Management of Patellar Tendinopathy in Athletes: A Narrative Review of Diagnosis, Treatment, and Return to Sport
creator: Yuhao Chen, Xin Kuang, Xinyan Zheng
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Highlights What are the main findings? Current evidence does not establish the superiority of any single exercise loading mode. Evidence for injection therapies varies across intervention types and is derived mainly from studies with short-term follow-up; whether any injection provides a sustained benefit beyond concurrent exercise remains uncertain, and current evidence does not support the use of extracorporeal shockwave therapy as a first-line or stand-alone intervention.Structural imaging findings may be associated with subsequent symptom development in selected populations, but their incremental value

title: Fatty acid synthase inhibition improves hypertension-induced erectile dysfunction by suppressing oxidative stress and NLRP3 inflammasome-dependent pyroptosis through activating the Nrf2/HO-1 pathway
creator: Jiaochen Luan, Mengchi Yu, Qi Gu, Xuan Zhou, Yunqiang Shao, Tong Chen, Jiayi Zhang, Zheng Zhu, Ninghong Song, Jie Yang
description: BackgroundErectile dysfunction (ED) is a prevalent male sexual disorder, commonly associated with hypertension, though the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood.ObjectiveThis study aims to explore the role of Fatty acid synthase (Fasn) in hypertension-induced ED and evaluate the therapeutic potential of the Fasn inhibitor C75.

title: Alpha-Asarone Ameliorates Dry Age-Related Macular Degeneration by Modulating the P2X7/NLRP3 Inflammasome Axis
creator: Xin Wang, Yuxiu Bi, Yuxiang Liu, Yao Nie, Junzhou Ding, Lei Yu, Shengjun Mao
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeTo examine whether α-asarone (ASA) protects dry age-related macular degeneration (dAMD) from sodium iodate (SI) injury by modulating the P2X7-mediated NLRP3 inflammasome axis.MethodsMale Sprague-Dawley rats were treated with SI to establish a dAMD model. Retinal structure and function were evaluated using electroretinography (ERG), optical coherence tomography (OCT), and hematoxylin-eosin staining, whereas the expression of functional and inflammatory proteins was analyzed via immunofluorescence and Western blotting.

title: Advancements in targeted and immunotherapy strategies for glioma: toward precision treatment
creator: Guangyuan Gong, Lang Jiang, Jing Zhou, Yuanchao Su
description: In recent years, significant breakthroughs have been made in cancer therapy, particularly with the development of molecular targeted therapies and immunotherapies, owing to advances in tumor molecular biology and molecular immunology. High-grade gliomas (HGGs), characterized by their high malignancy, remain challenging to treat despite standard treatment regimens, including surgery, radiotherapy, chemotherapy, and tumor treating fields (TTF).

title: Physical Parameters Influencing the Rate of Subretinal Injection: A Microfluidic Analysis
creator: Aaron Nagiel, Lamberto Rondoni
description: PurposeSubretinal injection during vitrectomy has become an important technique owing to the growing number of cell and gene therapy trials for retinal disease. Reducing the injection rate can mitigate trauma or shear forces on the retinal pigment epithelium, yet many surgeons alter the subretinal injection system in ways that could influence this rate.

title: Editorial: Binge drinking in the adolescent and young brain, volume II
creator: Eduardo López-Caneda, Séverine Lannoy, Salvatore Campanella, Carina Carbia
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). nd psychological problems (Babor et al., 2022). In this sense, alcohol misuse is recognized as being responsible for 3 million fatalities every year-around 4% of all deaths globally (World Health Organization, 2018). This percentage markedly increases in the American and European youth, where alcohol is associated with nearly three in 10 deaths in people aged 15–29 years (World Health Organization, 2011).

title: Case report: Overlapping syndrome of MOG-IgG associated optic neuritis and autoimmune encephalitis with co-existence of anti-NMDAR and anti-GABABR antibodies
creator: Zhujun Mei, Jingguo Wang, Junling Wang, Xiaoni Liu, Bo Deng, Wenbo Yang, Xiang Zhang, Xiangjun Chen, Hai Yu
description: We report a case of optic neuritis (ON) secondary to autoimmune encephalitis (AE) in a patient with concomitant antibodies to N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (NMDAR), gamma-aminobutyric acid-B receptor (GABABR), and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG). The patient exhibited a constellation of symptoms, including vision loss, seizures, mental and behavioral disorders, cognitive impairment, and speech abnormalities.

title: Disseminated Mixed Lytic‐Sclerotic Skeletal Metastases as Initial Presentation of Gallbladder Carcinoma: A Case Report
creator: Shivali Rao, Binaya Adhikari, Abhikanta Khatiwada
description: Gallbladder carcinoma is an aggressive malignancy often diagnosed at an advanced stage. Skeletal metastasis, especially mixed lytic‐sclerotic lesions, is rare and typically occurs late. This report highlights an unusual presentation where widespread bony metastases were the initial manifestation, leading to the diagnosis of gallbladder carcinoma.

title: Interactions between multi-species marine predator aggregations and the energy landscape
creator: Yannis P Papastamatiou, Johann Mourier, Gil Iosilevskii
description: Multi-species predator aggregations can be found in both coastal and pelagic ecosystems, forming for both foraging and refuging (resting) purposes. The energy landscape represents the power costs required to move through or reside within a habitat. As species may differ in their morphology, buoyancy and length, there may be species-specific heterogeneity in their energy landscapes.

title: Efficacy and safety of hemoporfin photodynamic therapy in treating port-wine stains in Chinese children: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Jing Xu, Hongxin Li
description: ObjectiveThe purpose of this study is to explore the efficacy and safety of hematoporphyrin monomethyl ether mediated photodynamic therapy (HMME-PDT) in treating children with port-wine stains (PWS).MethodLiterature related to the topic was searched in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang, and China Science Technology Journal Database online databases.

title: ADS024, a single-strain live biotherapeutic product of Bacillus velezensis alleviates dextran sulfate-mediated colitis in mice, protects human colonic epithelial cells against apoptosis, and maintains epithelial barrier function
creator: Sophie Irwin, Andrea Chupina Estrada, Becca Nelson, Ashlen Bullock, Berkeley Limketkai, Wendy Ho, Susan Acton, Laurent Chesnel, Hon Wai Koon
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Epithelial cell apoptosis and compromised gut barrier function are features of inflammatory bowel disease. ADS024 is a single-strain live biotherapeutic product (LBP) of Bacillus velezensis under development for treating ulcerative colitis (UC). The cytoprotective effects of the sterile filtrate of ADS024’s secreted products on UC patient-derived colonic tissues, human primary colonic epithelial cells (HPEC), and human colonic epithelial T84 cells were evaluated.

title: Case Report: Neonatal onset intractable diarrhea and hypoproteinemia due to intestinal malrotation and chronic midgut volvulus
creator: Cuifang Zheng, Song Sun, Ying Gong, Shijian Miao, Kuiran Dong, Ying Huang
description: Congenital diarrhea and enteropathies (CODEs) are a rare heterogeneous group of inherited disorders that typically present with severe chronic diarrhea during the first weeks of life. As a broad range of illnesses can present similarly in infants, establishing a definitive cause for CODEs is challenging.

title: Escalating competition in changing seas: baleen whales exploit killer whale prey herding
creator: Eve Jourdain, Chérine Baumgartner, David Cade, Paolo Domenici
description: Climate change and other anthropogenic pressures are rapidly reshaping marine ecosystems, altering prey availability and predator interactions. Yet empirical evidence of how these relationships shift under changing conditions remains scarce. Drawing on over a decade of monitoring in a subarctic fjord system, we provide a rare insight into these dynamics.

title: Mobile-based in-home telerehabilitation compared with in-hospital face-to-face rehabilitation for elderly patients after total hip arthroplasty in China's level 1 trauma center: a noninferiority randomized controlled trial
creator: Yang Zhou, Yiming Lyu, Qiaojie Wang, Yanhong Ma, Lihua Huang, Xin Zhang
description: BackgroundTelerehabilitation is gaining popularity in European and American countries, but whether it can be successfully implemented in China still lacks support from clinical studies.ObjectiveThis trial aimed to determine if a home-based telerehabilitation method is clinically noninferior to standard in-hospital face-to-face rehabilitation for elderly patients with total hip arthroplasty (THA) in China.

title: Effects of Cucurbita pepo seed extract on behavioral and neuroinflammatory changes in D-galactose-induced brain model
creator: Minza Saher, Aisha Aziz, Saba Majeed, Arzoo Ajaz, Sabiha Gul, Somia Gul
description: BackgroundAging is associated with progressive neuronal dysfunction driven by oxidative stress and neuroinflammation. Cucurbita pepo L. (pumpkin) is rich in bioactive compounds, including phenolics, flavonoids, carotenoids, tocopherols, and unsaturated fatty acids, with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. These characteristics suggest that C. pepo may have a neuroprotective role against age-related neuronal damage.

title: Chinese translation and validation of the Near-Death Experience Content scale
creator: Yan Li, Yan Chen, Charlotte Martial, Mingquan Shen, Héléna Cassol, Jing Yu, Xingyue Zhou, Chengcheng Ni, Meiqi Li, Nantu Hu, Olivia Gosseries, Steven Laureys, Haibo Di
description: IntroductionIn recent years, a growing number of near-death experience (NDE) testimonies have been collected worldwide due to an increasing interest in research on this phenomenon. China has many patients who survive life-threatening situations, leaving over much data on NDEs to be collected for research.

title: Correction to: The utility of endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration and robotic surgery for submucosal-type metastatic rectal cancer with persistent descending mesocolon
creator: Unknown
description: cancer with persistent descending mesocolon, Journal of Surgical Case Reports, Volume 2026, Issue 6, June 2026, rjag512, https://doi.org/10.1093/jscr/rjag512 In the originally published version of this manuscript the authors missed to acknowledge the contributions of Ayumi Ito, Institute of Gastroenterology, Department of Internal Medicine, Tokyo Women’s Medical University. The authors regret this oversight.

title: Generation of bovine decellularized testicular bio-scaffolds as a 3D platform for testis bioengineering
creator: Francesca Di Filippo, Tiziana A. L. Brevini, Georgia Pennarossa, Fulvio Gandolfi
description: Accelerating the genetic selection to obtain animals more resilient to climate changes, and with a lower environmental impact, would greatly benefit by a substantial shortening of the generation interval. One way to achieve this goal is to generate male gametes directly from embryos.

title: Rectourethral fistula with combined bladder-neck and rectal injury after holmium laser enucleation of the prostate: staged multidisciplinary reconstruction
creator: Yahya Ghazwani, Zeyad Alkhenizan, Abdulmalik Faqihi, Sultan Alhadi, Faisal Alrabah, Naif Alanazi
description: Rectourethral fistula after holmium laser enucleation of the prostate (HoLEP) is exceptionally rare. A man in his early 80s presented four days after HoLEP with urine per anus and fecal urethral catheter drainage. CT showed anterior rectal and bladder-base defects with pelvic collections. Emergency laparotomy achieved source control with bladder closure, suprapubic drainage, and colostomy.

title: Nanotechnological innovations in paediatric tuberculosis management: current trends and future prospects
creator: Taiwo Oreoluwa Ajayi, Madan Sai Poka, Bwalya Angel Witika
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Paediatric Tuberculosis (TB) continues to be a major global cause of morbidity and mortality. Children are more prone to contracting TB, which can spread quickly to extrapulmonary infection sites. Although the pathophysiology of the disease, drug pharmacokinetics, and the therapeutic window in children differ from those of adults, the same drugs used to treat adult TB have long been utilised to treat paediatric TB infections.

title: Deciphering cellular complexity: advances and future directions in single-cell protein analysis
creator: Qirui Zhao, Shan Li, Leonard Krall, Qianyu Li, Rongyuan Sun, Yuqi Yin, Jingyi Fu, Xu Zhang, Yonghua Wang, Mei Yang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Single-cell protein analysis has emerged as a powerful tool for understanding cellular heterogeneity and deciphering the complex mechanisms governing cellular function and fate. This review provides a comprehensive examination of the latest methodologies, including sophisticated cell isolation techniques (Fluorescence-Activated Cell Sorting (FACS), Magnetic-Activated Cell Sorting (MACS), Laser Capture Microdissection (LCM), manual cell picking, and microfluidics) and advanced approaches for protein profiling and protein-protein interaction analysis.

title: Editorial: Cytoskeletal alterations in aging and disease
creator: Monika S. Brill, Coralie Fassier, Yuyu Song
description: al functions critical for neuronal development and maintenance (Iwanski and Kapitein; Dent and Baas, 2014; Coles and Bradke, 2015; Yuan et al., 2017). Not surprisingly, dysfunction of any of these components can cause neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer’s, Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT) or Hereditary spastic Paraplegia (HSP) (Martnez-Hernandez et al.; Morris and Brady; Bomont et al.

title: Successful management of high-risk proliferative diabetic retinopathy during pregnancy with intravitreal faricimab
creator: Sonia Scallon, Michael Rauser, Anny M S Cheng, Kakarla V Chalam
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Management of proliferative diabetic retinopathy during pregnancy requires balancing maternal vision preservation against uncertain fetal risks associated with intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapy. We report a 27-year-old woman with a chronic type 1 diabetes mellitus who presented at 28 weeks and 1 day of gestation with high-risk proliferative diabetic retinopathy and dense vitreous hemorrhage in the left eye, precluding panretinal photocoagulation.

title: Role of the ventral portion of intermediate arcopallium in stability of female Bengalese finch song preferences
creator: Austin Coulter, Jonathan F. Prather
description: The process of decision making is a complex procedure influenced by both external and internal conditions. Songbirds provide an excellent model to investigate the neural mechanisms of decision making, because females rely on acoustic signals called songs as important stimuli in directing their mate choice.

title: EZH2 mutation status predicts inferior outcomes after bendamustine‐based immunochemotherapy in frontline follicular lymphoma: A GELTAMO multicenter validation study
creator: Carolina Martínez‐Laperche, Pilar Lancho‐Lavilla, Antonio Gutiérrez, Antonio Salar, Javier López‐Jiménez, Blanca Ferrer‐Lores, Alicia Serrano, Ana Jiménez‐Ubieto, María Poza, Francisco Javier Díaz‐Crespo, Paula Fernández‐Caldas, Laura Sanz‐Villanueva, Javier Menárguez‐Palanca, Ismael Buño, María Gar
description: Pablo Silva‐de‐Tena, Ramón García‐Sanz, Miguel Alcoceba, Mariana Bastos‐Oreiro Published: 2026 Follicular lymphoma (FL) is the most common indolent lymphoma, 1 , 2 a biologically and clinically heterogeneous entity with a diverse genetic landscape and characterized by slowly progressive but relapsing clinical course.

title: Tele-ophthalmology as an effective triaging tool for acute ophthalmic concerns
creator: Natalie A. Townsend, Shalini Shah, Joshua Reyes, Justin H. Townsend, Alison Bozung, Giselle Ricur, Rami J. Aboumourad
description: IntroductionThe purpose of this study is to determine baseline demographics and utilization trend of an on-demand, synchronous tele-ophthalmology triage program in evaluating acute ophthalmic concerns during the COVID-19 Public Health Emergency.MethodsSetting: Single-center retrospective chart review of telemedicine visits conducted by ophthalmologists and optometrists from University of Miami’s Bascom Palmer Eye Institute. Patient population: 6227 patients comprised 7138 telehealth encounters.

title: Editorial: The relationship between diabetes and cancers and its underlying mechanisms, volume II
creator: Qiang Huo, Shuo Wang, Ying Hou, Reginald M. Gorczynski, Yining Shen, Bin Wang, Hanyi Ge, Tao Li
description: the globe, suggesting that there may be a potential relationship between DM and cancer morbidity or mortality (3, 4). Moreover, the association of DM with oral conditions has been studied for years (5, 6), and recent studies have demonstrated the possible linkage between DM and oral cancer (7, 8).

title: Evaluating the introduction of a practical thyroid ultrasound teaching session for medical students
creator: Isobel Austin, Catherine Denver, Twisha Girisankar, Titus Cvasciuc, Peter Ellis, Philip C Johnston
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and AimsThe use of thyroid ultrasound is gaining in popularity at postgraduate level. However, it has not been broadly incorporated into the UK undergraduate medical curriculum. Thyroid ultrasound can help augment students understanding of both anatomy and endocrinology. We aimed to embed a hands-on thyroid ultrasound practical teaching session as part of the QUB (Queen’s University Belfast) 3rd year medical students’ endocrine and diabetes rotation.

title: Editorial: Global excellence in cellular neuropathology: Ukraine
creator: Andrii Cherninskyi, Dirk M. Hermann, Elena Lukyanetz, Oleg Krishtal
description: h Topic aims to show the diversity of modern research in the field of cellular neuroscience focusing on neuropathologies that are conducted in Ukrainian institutions. Neuroscience in Ukraine has a rich history, dating back to the establishment of St. Volodymyr University (now Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv) in 1834.

title: Predictive value of CT-based and AI-reconstructed 3D-TAPSE in patients undergoing transcatheter tricuspid valve repair
creator: Johannes Kirchner, Muhammed Gerçek, Hazem Omran, Kai Peter Friedrichs, Felix Rudolph, Tobias Rossnagel, Misagh Piran, Arseniy Goncharov, Maria Ivannikova, Volker Rudolph, Tanja Katharina Rudolph
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE) assessed by echocardiography has failed in predicting outcomes in patients with severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) undergoing transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention (TTVI). Considering the complex shape of the tricuspid annulus and right ventricle, as well as the difficult echocardiographic image acquisition of the right heart, cardiac computed tomography (CT) might be superior for the analysis of the annular excursion.

title: The key mechanism of pulsed electric field in inhibiting the flavor deterioration of whole egg liquid: Targeted regulation of chemical oxidation and microbial succession
creator: Liu Dong, Enhui Ma, Renrui Zheng, Jun Jiang, Xinqing Lu, Lili Zhang, Songyi Lin
description: This study elucidated mechanisms of pulsed electric field (PEF, 30 kV/cm, 100 Hz) and pasteurization (65 °C, 4 min) in inhibiting flavor deterioration of whole egg liquid. PEF extended shelf life to 36 days versus 20 days for pasteurization, with stable physicochemical property (P < 0.05). GC-IMS identified 90 compounds. By combined VIP > 1 and ROAV ≥0.

title: The sex effect on balance control while standing on vestibular-demanding tasks with/without vestibular simulations: implication for sensorimotor training for future space missions
creator: Li Zhang, Chao Qin, Jung Hung Chien
description: Background: Anatomical differences between sexes in the vestibular system have been reported. It has also been demonstrated that there is a sex difference in balance control while standing on vestibular-demanding tasks. In 2024, NASA expects to send the first female to the Moon.

title: Combined Effects of Beetle Density and Sex Ratio on Reproductive Trade‐Offs and Dung Burial in Tunnelling Dung Beetles
creator: Zinat Jahan Chowdhury, Zac Hemmings, Alfonsina Arriaga‐Jimenez, Karl Vernes, Timothy M. Schaerf, Nigel R. Andrew
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Dung beetle density and sex ratio play a significant role in intraspecific competition, and reproductive success depends on the beetle's maturity. We examined the impact of increasing density in small groups on dung burial and brood production using mature first‐generation individuals of two dung beetle species ( Onthophagus binodis and Digitonthophagus gazella) by manipulating the number of males and females in a dung pat. Beetles were reared under controlled laboratory conditions and provided with cattle dung, which was collected from pastureland.

title: Sirtuins mediate mitochondrial quality control mechanisms: a novel therapeutic target for osteoporosis
creator: Tianchi Zhang, Lining Wang, Xiping Duan, Yuanyuan Niu, Muzhe Li, Li Yun, Haitao Sun, Yong Ma, Yang Guo
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Mitochondria plays a role in cell differentiation and apoptosis processes. Maintaining mitochondrial function is critical, and this involves various aspects of mitochondrial quality control such as protein homeostasis, biogenesis, dynamics, and mitophagy. Osteoporosis, a metabolic bone disorder, primarily arises from two factors: the dysregulation between lipogenic and osteogenic differentiation of aging bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells, and the imbalance between osteoblast-mediated bone formation and osteoclast-mediated bone resorption. Mitochondrial quality control has the potential to mitigate or even reverse the effects.

title: Flushing Strategies for Totally Implantable Venous Access Devices in Nurse‐Led Cancer Care: Exploratory Randomized Clinical Trial
creator: Chi‐Jia Ho, Jason Chia‐Hsun Hsieh, Hui (Grace) Xu, Chieh‐Ching Yen, Hsuan‐Chih Kuo, Chih‐Ting Chou, Li‐Chin Chen, Bo‐Cyuan Wang
description: Aim (s)To examine catheter‐related complications across different flushing strategies for totally implantable venous access devices when care is delivered through a standardized, nurse‐led, protocol‐driven framework.DesignA single‐center, prospective, exploratory, randomized, single‐blind, three‐arm parallel‐group clinical trial.ResultsAmong 192 participants, catheter‐related complications were rare across all groups.

title: Clinical Decision Support for Fall Prevention in Primary Care
creator: Nancy K. Latham, Erin Hommel, Mackenzie Kiesman, Stuart R. Lipsitz, David W. Bates, Diane L. Carroll, Alexandra C. Frost, Pamela M. Garabedian, Julia V. Loewenthal, Michael Sainlaire, Lipika Samal, Wenyu Song, Matthew Wien, Patricia C. Dykes
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Key PointsQuestionDoes an electronic health record–integrated clinical decision support intervention reduce falls among older adults in primary care?FindingsIn this cluster randomized clinical trial of 11 945 patients, there was a modest but statistically significant reduction in the rate per 100 patient-years of 1 or more International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision–coded falls (including falls with injuries) over the study period in patients from intervention vs control practices.MeaningThe findings of this study suggest that an electronic health record–integrated

title: Curvilinear association between Framingham Steatosis Index and chronic kidney disease: a nationwide cross-sectional study
creator: Chunqi Jiang, Bo Wang, Jun Wang, Yinuo Qu, Xin Zhang
description: IntroductionFatty liver disease is potentially linked to chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet the association between the Framingham Steatosis Index (FSI) and CKD remains uncharted. Our study thoroughly investigated the correlation between FSI and CKD, aiming to elucidate the underlying links between these two conditions.

title: Is cardiovascular autonomic control during the day‐to‐night transition dependent on dim light melatonin onset? An exploratory analysis in healthy adults
creator: Leandro C Brito, Megan Jones, Caroline P Garcês, Steven A Shea, Saurabh S Thosar
description: We tested whether dim‐light melatonin onset (DLMO) is time‐aligned with the transition between biological day into night in cardiovascular autonomic control (CV onset time). We studied 10 healthy adults (4 females, age 25 ± SD 2 years) under an ultra‐short semi‐constant routine protocol (<8lux). Participants remained seated for 7 h until 1 h after their habitual bedtime.

title: Unravelling the impact of SARS-CoV-2 on hemostatic and complement systems: a systems immunology perspective
creator: Didar Murad, Rehan Zafar Paracha, Maryum Nisar
description: The hemostatic system prevents and stops bleeding, maintaining circulatory integrity after injury. It directly interacts with the complement system, which is key to innate immunity. In coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), dysregulation of the hemostatic and complement systems has been associated with several complications.

title: Chronic Limb‐Threatening Ischemia Shows No Adaptability of Mitochondrial Function After Revascularisation
creator: Fiona Speichinger, Alexandra Gratl, Ben Raude, Marco Arndt, Nina A. Hering, Andreas Greiner, Dominik Pesta, Christian Schineis, Jan Paul Frese
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) impairs limb perfusion, leading to myopathy characterised by altered mitochondrial content and respiration. Because ischemic muscle appears to adapt differently across PAD stages, we examined stage‐specific skeletal‐muscle mitochondrial function before and after successful revascularisation. Muscle biopsies of gastrocnemius and vastus lateralis muscle were obtained from 32 patients—21 with intermittent claudication (IC) and 11 with chronic limb‐threatening ischemia (CLTI)—before and 6 weeks after successful revascularisation. Mitochondrial respiration was assessed by high resolution respirometry (HRR).

title: Prevalence, risk and resilience factors of mental health conditions among female sex workers: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Olivia Kalinowski, Anastasiia Lotysh, Gizem Kaya, Franziska Kroehn-Liedtke, Lena Karoline Zerbe, Hristiana Mihaylova, Krisztina Sipos, Wulf Rössler, Meryam Schouler-Ocak
description: IntroductionFemale sex workers are a vulnerable hard-to-reach group. Research in this field is scarce due to several issues, such as methodological difficulties or societal stigmatization. Most of the available literature focuses on sexually transmittable diseases. This review and meta-analysis aim to compile literature on the mental health of female sex workers.

title: Management of extravasations of enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab: a case report and mini review of the current literature
creator: Hendrik Dinkel, Konstantin E. Seifert, Martin Bögemann, Andres J. Schrader, Katrin Schlack
description: Following the EV-302/KEYNOTE-A39 study, the combination therapy of enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (EV-P) has been established as a new first-line treatment for metastatic urothelial carcinoma. With increasing use, the documentation and publication of unexpected side effects and complications are essential to systematize procedures.

title: Low-dose intranasal deferoxamine modulates memory, neuroinflammation, and the neuronal transcriptome in the streptozotocin rodent model of Alzheimer’s disease
creator: Jared M. Fine, Jacob Kosyakovsky, Tate T. Bowe, Katherine A. Faltesek, Benjamin M. Stroebel, Juan E. Abrahante, Michael R. Kelly, Elizabeth A. Thompson, Claire M. Westby, Kiley M. Robertson, William H. Frey, Leah R. Hanson
description: IntroductionIntranasal (IN) deferoxamine (DFO) has emerged over the past decade as a promising therapeutic in preclinical experiments across neurodegenerative and neurovascular diseases. As an antioxidant iron chelator, its mechanisms are multimodal, involving the binding of brain iron and the consequent engagement of several pathways to counter pathogenesis across multiple diseases.

title: Symptom Profiles Compatible With Disorders of Gut‐Brain Interaction in Individuals With Coeliac Disease on a Long‐Term Gluten‐Free Diet
creator: Tom van Gils, Hans Törnblom, Floris van Overveld, Olafur S Palsson, Ami D Sperber, Shrikant I Bangdiwala, Inês A Trindade, Marc A Benninga, Gerd Bouma, Magnus Simrén
description: BackgroundPersistent gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms are frequently reported in patients with coeliac disease (CD). Knowledge about the role of disorders of gut‐brain interaction (DGBI) as the cause of these persistent symptoms remains limited.ObjectiveTo assess the prevalence and factors associated with DGBI‐compatible symptom profiles in individuals with CD on a long‐term gluten‐free diet (GFD).

title: Transition From Child to Adult Care in Paediatric Neurological Disorders in Europe—A Joint EAN‐EPNS Survey of Current Practices for Healthcare Providers
creator: Dana Craiu, Cristina Cazacu, Maria T Papadopoulou, Ming Lim, Kevin Rostasy, Anna C Jansen, Leena M Haataja, Ilona Anna Kopyta, Kristl G Claeys, Guido Rubboli, Chiara Ferrazzoli, Ronan McGinty, Maria Roberta Cilio, Maria Lolich, Dimitrios Zafeiriou, Nadia Bahi‐Buisson, Elena Moro, Gereon R Fink, Thom
description: BackgroundTransition from paediatric to adult care is essential for young people with paediatric‐onset neurological disorders, yet remains inconsistently structured across Europe. This study aimed to characterise current transition practices, identify key barriers and explore perceived priorities for improving transition care.

title: Clinical significance of anti-Epstein–Barr virus antibodies in systemic chronic active Epstein–Barr virus disease
creator: Miwako Nishio, Minori Saito, Mayumi Yoshimori, Yuki Kumaki, Ayaka Ohashi, Eri Susaki, Ichiro Yonese, Megumi Sawada, Ayako Arai
description: Systemic chronic active Epstein–Barr virus disease (sCAEBV) is a rare and fatal neoplasm, involving clonally proliferating Epstein–Barr virus (EBV)-infected T cells or natural killer cells. Patients with sCAEBV have abnormal titers of anti-EBV antibodies in their peripheral blood, but their significance is unknown.

title: Prognostication in emergency room patients: comparing ultrasensitive and contemporary quantification of cardiac troponin levels below the 99th percentile
creator: Anna Carrasquer, Germán Cediel, Alma Gómez-Sanz, Óscar M. Peiró, Isabel Fort-Gallifa, Alfredo Bardaji, Jose Luis Ferreiro
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionCardiac troponin levels below the 99th percentile improve the predictive efficacy for cardiovascular events when associated with relevant clinical variables. However, whether ultra-sensitive analytical methods improve this predictive efficacy over less sensitive or contemporary analytical methods remains unknown.MethodsThis retrospective observational study involved consecutive patients who presented to the emergency department for suspected acute coronary syndrome and underwent measurement of ultra-sensitive cardiac troponin I (Singulex) and contemporary cardiac troponin I (Siemens) with levels below the 99th percentile.

title: Bridging Critical Care and Mental Health: Jordanian ICU Nurses' Self‐Reported Knowledge, Skills, Attitudes and Confidence in Caring for Patients With Mental Illness
creator: Ahmad B. Al‐Rawashdeh, Mahmoud Abdel Hameed Shahin, Samia Eaid Elgazzar, Ateya Megahed Ibrahim, Rasha Mohammed Hussien
description: BackgroundIntensive Care Unit (ICU) nurses frequently care for patients with mental illness, yet many report feeling insufficiently prepared to address mental health needs in critical care settings. Understanding nurses' knowledge, skills and attitudes toward mental health care is essential to improving the quality and safety of care.

title: Locally Estimated Scatterplot Smoothing for Censored Survival Data
creator: David van Klaveren, Peter C. Austin, Patrick W. Serruys, Ben van Calster, Frank E. Harrell
description: In the absence of censoring, locally estimated scatterplot smoothing (LOESS) is a powerful tool to estimate the relationship between a continuous covariate and the probability of an event and is often used to visually assess calibration of prognostic models. Since follow‐up in prognostic studies is often incomplete, we aimed to study the extension of LOESS to right‐censored data.

title: Evaluation of proline-rich antimicrobial peptides as potential lead structures for novel antimycotics against Cryptococcus neoformans
creator: Alexandra Brakel, Thomas Grochow, Stefanie Fritsche, Daniel Knappe, Andor Krizsan, Simone A. Fietz, Gottfried Alber, Ralf Hoffmann, Uwe Müller
description: BackgroundCryptococcosis and cryptococcal meningitis, caused by Cryptococcus neoformans infections, lead to approximately 180,000 deaths per year, primarily in developing countries. Individuals with compromised immune systems, e.g., due to HIV infection (AIDS) or chemotherapy, are particularly vulnerable. Conventional treatment options are often limited and can cause severe side effects.

title: Successful management of coagulation dysfunction in a patient with fulminant myocarditis: a case report
creator: Shanshan Dong, Qi Peng, Kai Lu, Qimei Wei, Jun Yang
description: Fulminant myocarditis (FM) is an acute, diffuse inflammatory myocardial disease characterized by abrupt onset and extremely rapid progression. Patients typically exhibit haemodynamic abnormalities that may lead to respiratory failure, liver and renal failure, and subsequent coagulopathy. Collectively, these complications significantly increase the risk of early mortality.

title: Antimicrobial resistance, serogroups, virulence gene profiles and MLST of Escherichia coli from giant panda
creator: Mingxi Li, Ruiqing Lv, Xiaowei Li, Chao Song, Liang Xingxin, Huanrong Zhang
description: Escherichia coli is a major bacterial pathogen which causes diarrhea in the giant panda. This study investigated the biological characteristics of 100 E. coli strains isolated from fecal samples collected from 100 captive giant pandas of different age groups and sexes.

title: To Test or Not to Test: A Real‐World Study of Employee Views and Decision‐Making for Genetic Testing in the Workplace
creator: Katherine Hendy, Rebecca Ferber, Subhamoy Pal, Sarah McCain, Alyx Vogle, Jonathan M. Reader, Elizabeth Charnysh, W. Gregory Feero, Anya E. R. Prince, Kunal Sanghavi, Alexandra Truhlar, Drew Blasco, Veda N. Giri, Charles Lee, J. Scott Roberts, Wendy R. Uhlmann, the INSIGHT @ Work Consortium
description: BackgroundThis study explored employees' decision‐making processes and perspectives on workplace genetic testing (wGT), comparing those who had not participated (Non‐Testers) with those who had participated (Testers) in wGT.MethodsEmployees at a large US healthcare system offering wGT were recruited via email and onsite advertising and surveyed. The web survey assessed respondent demographics, information‐seeking activities, and perceived benefits and risks of wGT.

title: Serological, phenotypic and molecular characterization of brucellosis in small ruminants in northern Algeria
creator: Ibrahim Nabi, Rachid Achek, Abdelkadir Karim, Falk Melzer, Hanka Brangsch, Mandy C. Elschner, Heinrich Neubauer, Hosny El-Adawy
description: Brucellosis is considered a common bacterial zoonotic disease of high prevalence in countries of the Middle East and the Mediterranean region with economic and public health impact. The present study aimed to investigate the current situation of brucellosis in small ruminants reared in Médéa and Sidi Bel-Abbès provinces, north Algeria.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Supramolecular Salicylic Acid Peeling Combined With Intense Pulsed Light Versus Intense Pulsed Light Monotherapy in Erythematotelangiectatic‐Predominant Rosacea: A Retrospective Real‐World Comparative Study
creator: Birao Fan, Ruixing Yu
description: BackgroundEvidence is limited on whether supramolecular salicylic acid (SSA) peeling adds benefit to intense pulsed light (IPL) for erythematotelangiectatic‐predominant rosacea in routine practice. We compared real‐world effectiveness and short‐term safety of SSA + IPL versus IPL monotherapy using objective imaging and patient‐centered outcomes.

title: Case report: Efgartigimod is a novel therapeutic option for ocular myasthenia gravis: a report of 2 cases
creator: Tianying Ma, Ying Zhu, Ruixia Zhu
description: IntroductionEfgartigimod has been approved for the treatment of acetylcholine receptor antibodies-positive generalized myasthenia gravis (AChR-Ab+gMG), but its efficacy in patients with ocular myasthenia gravis (OMG) is not known.Case presentationWe describe 2 cases of patients with AChR-Ab+ OMG who showed unfavorable responses to corticosteroids and tacrolimus.

title: Case report: A rollercoaster journey of pemphigus vegetans
creator: Xiaoyuan Hou, Jia Chen
description: Pemphigus vegetans (P Veg), the rarest subtype of pemphigus, is characterized by vegetative plaques, primarily affecting intertriginous areas. The most common autoantibodies target desmoglein 3 (Dsg3). A 60-year-old female patient presented with well-demarcated red vegetative plaques on her feet, vulva, and thigh, accompanied by surrounding pustules.

title: Machine Learning in Dementia Research: Trends, Biomarkers, Prediction Goals, and Data Modalities
creator: Yao‐Chin Wang, Hsien Chang Yeh, Md. Mohaimenul Islam, Woon‐Man Kung
description: ObjectiveMachine learning (ML) is increasingly used in dementia research for diagnosis, early detection, prognosis, biomarker characterization, and disease phenotyping. This study aimed to provide a bibliometric and thematic overview of ML applications in dementia, emphasizing biological mechanisms, prediction goals, data modalities, collaborative networks, and emerging computational approaches.

title: Factors driving FIFA world cup 2022 viewership ratings in mainland China: marketing outlooks for FIFA world cup 2026
creator: Zongqing Wang, Lide Su, Agudamu, Tao Gong, Te Bu, Yang Zhang
description: IntroductionThe FIFA World Cup is not only the most lucrative athletic event globally, but it also functions as a platform for promoting peace owing to FIFA's new vision. Nevertheless, the determinants of TV viewership ratings, especially in the Chinese market, which is a critical revenue stream for FIFA TV broadcasting, are still unsolved.

title: Nervonic Acid Promotes Skin Regeneration by Enhancing Collagen Synthesis and Suppressing Inflammation
creator: Soobeen Chung, Sun Jeong Kim, Sun Jae Kwon, Hong Bae Jeon, Sang Eon Park, Jong Wook Chang
description: BackgroundSkin regeneration is a fundamental biological process that restores tissue integrity and functional homeostasis following tissue injury. Beyond its essential role as a barrier against environmental stressors, effective skin regeneration is critically relevant to aesthetic outcomes and the modulation of cutaneous aging. Nervonic acid (NA) promotes angiogenesis, supports nerve fiber regeneration, and suppresses pro‐inflammatory signaling pathways.

title: Maternal diet in pregnancy and acute leukemia in infants: a case-control study in Mexico City
creator: María Luisa Pérez-Saldivar, M. Karen Flores-García, Nancy Núñez-Villegas, Arturo Fajardo-Gutiérrez, Aurora Medina-Sanson, Elva Jiménez-Hernández, Jorge Alfonso Martín-Trejo, Norma López-Santiago, José Gabriel Peñaloza-González, Beatriz Cortés-Herrera, Laura Elizabeth Merino-Pasaye, Raquel Amador-Sán
description: IntroductionEpidemiological studies around the world on acute leukemia (AL) and risk factors in infants are scarce. Infant AL has been proposed to originate in utero, which facilitates its study by establishing a short exposure time in pregnant women to environmental and dietary factors that could contribute to the risk of or protection against leukemia.

title: Insight Into the Genetic Architecture of Local (Mal)Adaptation in Wild and Feral Brassica rapa Populations
